morgan: Heads up — bringing up Helios-13B (open checkpoint) for production. Quick proposal for the quant/bring‑up path: run three parallel experiments to understand the quality vs cost tradeoffs and pick a safe default rollout. 1) INT8 (symmetric) per-layer calibration using KL + minmax for outliers. 2) FP8 (e4m3-like) with dynamic range scaling. 3) Hybrid: 4-bit for attention kernels + INT8 for FF, to test extreme cost wins.

morgan: Goals: keep production-quality regressions small (target deltas below thresholds), measure latency and token cost vis-a-vis our FP16 baseline, and produce a canary + rollback plan. Looking for owners for the runs and checklists. :eyes:

alejandra: sgtm. can you add numeric targets? what is acceptable quality drop per eval?

morgan: Target thresholds: <=2% BLEU drop on codebench, <=1.5% ROUGE on summarization, <=0.75% instruction-follower error. Latency target: <1.8x FP16 p99. Cost: aim for <=0.6x token cost. If INT8 violates quality, escalate to FP8, then hybrid.

sam: I can own the per-layer calibration INT8 experiments. Which calibration corpus should we use? size and composition?

morgan: Use the new helios-calib-v2 set: 8k in-domain prompts (mix of code, dialogue, summarization) + 2k edge cases. s3 path: s3://redwood-ci/helios/calib-v2.tar.gz. Keep an OOD subset of 1k for stress.

ryan: Add eval buckets: summarization, code-gen, dialog, instruction-following. Run automated eval harness and produce a table with metric deltas + significance. Also add a small human eval sample.

tia: Important: ensure compilation step supports quant-aware dtypes. For FP8 runs avoid fused custom kernels initially — run in conservative mode so we can attribute regressions to quantization not kernel fusion. Also capture activation histograms and per-layer scaling factors.

quant-lab-bot: Note: gguf converter supports flags --quantize-activations --calib-method=kl --per-channel. Recommend using --safe-fallback to keep fp16 for layers that fail calibration thresholds.

morgan: Example calibration command I'm going to push (INT8 per-layer KL):

```bash
# per-layer KL calibration (INT8 symmetric)
python tools/quant_calib.py \
  --model checkpoints/helios-13b \
  --calib-set s3://redwood-ci/helios/calib-v2.tar.gz \
  --method kl \
  --per-channel \
  --out checkpoints/helios-13b-int8-kl
```

sam: I'll run that on dedicated g5x2 pool (gpool-dedicated-42). ETA ~6h. I'll post the run id and logs.

ryan: When a quant checkpoint is produced, create two eval jobs: `micro-regressions` (fast unit metrics + perf) and `production-sweep` (full eval suites + small human sample). Tag the artifacts and link them to PR/issue. Include throughput (tokens/s), mem footprint, and latency p50/p95/p99.

alejandra: please add a mandatory 200-sample human review for instruction-following; label whether outputs are ``acceptable / borderline / broken``. We should fail the rollout if >1% are "broken" compared to baseline.

tia: Canary policy suggestion: route 1% traffic to the quant variant for 24h, with spike detectors on error-rate, hallucination signals, and latency. Auto-fallback to fp16 if error spikes >0.5% or latency >2x baseline.

morgan: I'll add onboarding README updates: checklist items will include calibration script, eval runs with buckets, human eval, perf tables, canary config, rollback plan, and gguf/edge export notes. I'll also add an entry in the model metadata for which quant strategy is the chosen default and why.

devops-bot: Deploy job scheduled: gpool-dedicated-42, start-time 2026-03-05T18:20:00Z, job-id run-1768456789-gpool

sam: Done. Uploaded results to /runs/1768456789/ with artifacts: calib-metrics.json, per-layer-hists.tar.gz, quant-checkpoint.pt, perf-summary.csv. Created issue ML-4312 with logs and links.

ryan: I'll review the artifact set and sanity-check the human eval tomorrow. Thanks all for the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
